definition: The electrostatic forces of attraction between the positive ions and the delocalised electrons, which hold the giant metallic lattice together.
msAccepts: electrostatic forces/attraction between positive ions and delocalised electrons
attraction between the lattice of positive ions and the sea of delocalised electrons
msAvoids: sharing of electron pairs between metal atoms
a bond between two metal ions

definition: An outer-shell electron that is no longer attached to any particular atom or bond and can move freely throughout the whole metallic structure.
msAccepts: electrons free to move through the whole structure
not attached to any particular atom or pair of atoms
msAvoids: electrons that have left the metal
free electrons (as a definition — name them delocalised)

definition: A regular arrangement of particles repeated in three dimensions. A metallic lattice is a regular arrangement of positive ions with delocalised electrons between them.
msAccepts: regular repeating arrangement of ions in three dimensions

definition: Can be hammered or bent into different shapes without shattering. Metals are malleable because layers of positive ions slide over each other while the bonding stays intact.
msAccepts: layers of ions slide over each other without the bonding breaking
msAvoids: can be drawn into wires (that is ductile)

definition: Can be drawn out into wires. The explanation is the same as for malleability — the layers of ions slide past each other while the delocalised electrons keep the bonding intact.
msAccepts: can be drawn out into wires
msAvoids: the same property as malleability with no explanation
can be melted and poured into moulds
